item.title: Sanofi/Wave Genetic Disease Updates
item.description:
• Summary: Sanofi and Wave Life Sciences provided updates on their genetic disease programs, potentially ending a 40-year drought in the field. The partnership focuses on RNA-targeted therapies for rare genetic disorders.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: FierceBiotech

item.title: Novartis Terminates Plant Contract with Porton
item.description:
• Summary: Novartis terminated a plant contract with Chinese CDMO Porton, threatening $64 million in legal claims. The move reflects ongoing tensions in the pharmaceutical manufacturing supply chain.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: FiercePharma

item.title: Regeneron Parabilis Deal
item.description:
• Summary: Regeneron entered into a partnership with Parabilis to develop a new class of antibody‑drug conjugate (ADC) therapies. The deal could be worth up to $2.3 billion, including an upfront payment of $125 million. Parabilis brings its expertise in hard‑to‑target intracellular proteins, while Regeneron contributes its antibody and development capabilities.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Endpoints News, BioSpace, Fierce Biotech

item.title: Quince Reverse Merger
item.description:
• Summary: Cash‑strapped Quince Therapeutics, after a rare disease drug failure, found a path forward through a reverse merger. The deal provides a lifeline for the company, which had been struggling financially following the clinical setback.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech

item.title: Bristol-Myers Houston Manufacturing Plant
item.description:
• Summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb is exploring the construction of a $1 billion manufacturing facility in Houston, Texas. The plant would support the company's growing biologics portfolio and cell therapy production. The filing indicates a potential significant expansion of Bristol's manufacturing footprint.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma

item.title: Unlocking Value from Mature Drug Products
item.description:
• Summary: An article from BioPharma Dive discusses how pharmaceutical companies can unlock additional value from mature drug products through strategic outsourcing. The piece argues that by leveraging contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) for lifecycle management, companies can reduce costs, optimize supply chains, and extend the commercial viability of established brands. It provides a framework for evaluating which products are suitable for outsourcing and how to manage such partnerships effectively.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive
